title: Cache-aware fused dequant + attention kernels and schedule for tiled prefill/low-latency decode
creator: Sofia Martinez
description:
Background: Dequantization overhead has become a dominant cost for INT8/FP8 serving paths when bandwidth-limited or when KV cache layout forces extra memory traffic. Our prefill pipelines (long sequences, large batch) and decode pipelines (single-token, low latency) have divergent optimal kernel choices. This ticket designs and implements cache-aware fused kernels and a schedule/selector to reduce dequant memory traffic while preserving numeric stability.

Goals: 
- Implement fused dequant + matmul for attention key/query/value prefill steps to avoid write-back of wide FP16 tensors in the hot path.
- Add an alternative low-allocation decode kernel that performs lazy dequant only for the attended columns (sparse per-step dequant) to minimize latency for single-token decode.
- Extend kernel selector with a cost model that includes dequant bandwidth, L2/L3 cache pressure, and vectorized path suitability (int8 GEMM vs fp8 fused).
- Provide opt-in layer-level quantization metadata (per-layer scale & group-size) so the runtime can choose hybrid mixed-precision for sensitive layers.

Design decisions: 
- Fused kernels: Implement a fused pipeline that loads INT8 weights, applies group-wise dequant into a register/block-local buffer, and performs matmul accumulation directly into FP16/FP32 accumulators without writing a full dequantized tensor to DRAM. This reduces DRAM bandwidth at the cost of increased register usage and slightly larger kernel code size.
- Prefill vs Decode scheduling: Prefill uses throughput-oriented fused kernels with larger tiles (tileM=128, tileN=64 preferred on A100/H100) and aggregated KV writes for cache-friendly layout. Decode defaults to a micro-kernel that performs minimal dequant on-the-fly for the requested token indices and keeps KV cache in packed INT8 when possible.
- Fallbacks: For long-head sequences where accumulation error is high, runtime can fall back to FP16 dequant full-tensor write. We prefer this fallback only when quality regression threshold (measured by eval suite) exceeds 0.5% perplexity delta.
- Cache-awareness: Kernel selector uses telemetry counters: per-request sequence length distribution, batch-size histogram, recent L2 miss rates, and observed dequant CPU time. A simple heuristic cost model (bandwidth_cost = bytes_dequantized / effective_memory_bandwidth) + compute_cost estimates chooses kernels.

Implementation plan: 
1) Add baseline fused INT8->FP16 GEMM kernel prototype (PR: github.com/redwood/runtime/pull/3892).
2) Implement lazy-dequant decode path and packed-INT8 KV layout toggle.
3) Extend kernel registry and selector: new flags (supports_fused_dequant, kv_packed_compatible) and cost model parameters in config.
4) Add per-layer quant metadata in model manifest (group_size, scale_bytes, prefer_mixed_precision).
5) Run microbench harness across infra (A100, H100, T4) for prefill and decode scenarios; collect p99 latency, mean throughput, and SLO violation rates.

Benchmarks so far (local perf cluster): 
- Prefill (seq=2048, batch=8) on A100: fused path reduced end-to-end latency by 14% and reduced DRAM write traffic for prefill KV by ~42% vs naive dequant-then-gemm.
- Decode (single-token, beam=1) on A100: lazy-dequant microkernel reduced median latency by 9% and tail (p99) by 11% when KV cache remained in packed INT8 format.
- Numeric quality: FP8 per-layer mixed mode (sensitive layers FP16) showed <0.3% delta on our prompt evaluation set; pure INT8 had outliers in MMLU-like evaluations and needs per-layer overrides.

Rollout plan: 
- Stage 1 (canary): Enable fused prefill kernels for hosted runtime on a small fleet for paid workloads with no strict deterministic requirements. Provide opt-out flag.
- Stage 2 (wider): Allow private/dedicated customers to enable packed-INT8 KV cache and lazy-dequant decode via config.
- Stage 3: Add automatic rollout policies that switch to fallback FP16 per-layer when eval quality degrades.

Telemetry and metrics: Add counters exposed in Console: dequant_bytes_saved, fused_kernel_hit_ratio, avg_dequant_time_ms, quality_regressions_count. Tie regression alerts to Redwood Optimize evaluations.

Open questions / risks: 
- Kernel code size vs register pressure: fused kernels increased register spilling on some older GPUs (T4) causing worse performance; we must maintain a fallback path.
- Interaction with batching and continuous batching: fused kernels benefit when batching coalesces requests; decode single-token patterns may suffer. We will evaluate batching thresholds where fused wins.
- Security/compatibility: packed INT8 KV cache introduces a layout change; we must ensure migration and backward compatibility across running versions.

Artifacts: design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RUN/Fused-Dequant-Kernels , PR: https://github.com/redwood/runtime/pull/3892 , benchmark dashboard: https://dash.redwood.ai/runs/quant-fused-2026

Acceptance criteria: 
- Fused prefill path demonstrates >=10% median latency improvement or >=30% DRAM write reduction on A100 for seq>=1024 workloads in our perf suite.
- Lazy-dequant decode path reduces p99 by >=8% on single-token decode scenarios without quality regressions >0.5% on evaluation set.
- Kernel selector can make deterministic decisions based on config/telemetry and exposes debug traces for each request when debugging is enabled.
